messages:
alex: Quick sync — noticed a weird double-ownership metric spike on shard-7 after the last canary. looks like prefix handoff sometimes leaves a short window where both old and new host think they own the prefix.
priya: ugh. saw that too. traces show lease revocation RPCs succeeded but eviction still ran on old host. could be ordering with the residency flag flip.
matt: can you paste the trace id? i want to see the handshake ordering around the demote event.
alex: trace 0x9f3c. snippet: old host sends LEASE_RELEASE -> control plane ack -> new host commits PIN -> old host runs EVICT job and marks prefix free. but new host still reading/writing for ~200ms.
ken: suspected race: we treat commit as authoritative but evict is async and doesn't wait for readers to drain. we probably need a short grace period or a stronger handshake.
priya: options: 1) make demote blocking until no active readers (adds tail latency), 2) push grace window + quick retry on double-apply detection, 3) add sequenced epoch CAS on residency record so double-apply fails fast.
olga: preference for 2 + telemetry first. blocking demote would kill some tests. the grace window of 200-500ms seems reasonable for most workloads. also add a metric for "ownership-overlap-ms" to catch regressions.
alex: agree on telemetry-first. but we also need an API contract change for pin/unpin to expose a heartbeat or active-reader count for better heuristics. currently pin() only returns success/failure.
matt: sketching API:
```
// attempt to take ownership
TakePrefix(prefix, opts) -> {epoch, pinned, active_readers}
ReleasePrefix(prefix, epoch) -> {accepted}
```
if ReleasePrefix sees epoch mismatch -> it should reject and we log overlap.
ken: epoch CAS lets new host refuse to commit if it sees a stale epoch, preventing silent double-owned writes. small overhead but avoids most misorders.
priya: tradeoffs: epoch CAS requires central store or strong coord; that reintroduces dependency on k-v lease store. we already have control plane but want local-path fast common case.
olga: thought: have a hybrid: local fast path uses best-effort handshake plus ephemeral epoch; control plane does durable epoch only on contested transitions. adds complexity but keeps common-case perf.
alex: for correctness, we should treat eviction as idempotent but also add a prefix ownership state machine with explicit states: Owned -> Demoting -> FreePending -> Free. make demote wait for either active_readers==0 OR grace_timeout expiry.
matt: add instrumentation: demote_start_ts, demote_end_ts, readers_drain_time, evict_run_time, eviction_retries. these are cheap and will help tune grace window.
priya: also need tests: chaos test that injects delayed RPCs and asserts no dual-active-writer periods. and a canary that asserts "ownership-overlap-ms" < 50ms after rollout.
ken: implement idea: on demote, old host publishes a short-lived tombstone with epoch+deadline. new host on take will check for tombstone and either bump epoch or wait until deadline. that avoids central locking.
olga: love the tombstone pattern. less coupling and simple to implement in store. we should document the semantics in the handshake RFC update.
alex: next steps: ken, prototype tombstone + epoch CAS local-store PR. matt, add demote metrics and a lightweight test harness. priya, write the chaos test plan. olga, update RFC text and telemetry dashboard proposal. i'll coordinate canary gating.
infra-bot: deploy pipeline: created branch refs/prefix-handoff/tombstone-prototype by ken, triggered CI.
priya: timeline: aim for prototype in next week, metrics live in 2 weeks, canary after perf smoke.
alex: thanks team — let's keep messages in this thread for followups. :thumbsup:
